summary: This Makefile defines a set of commands for managing a Python application running in Docker. It sets up variables for Docker container configuration, environment files, and binaries, then provides convenient `make` commands for common tasks like building and running the container, opening shells, and running quality assurance tools like linting and type checking.

explanations.5: BIN is a variable storing the path where command-line tools (like Python linters) are installed inside the Docker container so we can reference them without typing the full path each time.
explanations.17: ENV is a shorthand variable that includes the --env-file flag pointing to our Docker environment file, so we can reuse it in multiple docker compose commands without repeating the full flag.
explanations.20: YAML is setting up the COMPOSE_FILE environment variable to tell Docker which compose configuration file to use; it's prefixed to commands so Docker knows which setup to apply.
explanations.23: _CYAN is a format string that uses escape codes to make text appear in cyan color when printed; it's used by the help command to highlight output.
explanations.27: DOCKER_VSCODE converts the container name into hexadecimal format (a special encoding) because VS Code's remote connection URI requires it to identify which container to attach to.
explanations.31: This runs a bash shell interactively (-it flags) inside the named Docker container, giving you direct command-line access to your application environment.
explanations.43: This tells VS Code to open and connect to the Docker container as a remote development environment, letting you edit and debug code as if it were running locally.
explanations.50: This uses awk (a text processing tool) to parse this Makefile itself, looking for lines with `##` comments, and prints them as a formatted help menu so users can see all available commands.
explanations.67: pydocstyle runs inside the container and checks whether the Python docstrings (documentation comments) follow proper formatting conventions.
explanations.72: Black is a Python code formatter that automatically reformats your code to follow a consistent style; the @ prefix hides the command itself from output.
explanations.77: pylint analyzes your Python code for bugs, style issues, and other problems without actually executing it, giving you a quality report.
explanations.82: mypy checks that your Python code uses types correctly (for example, that you're not passing a number where text is expected) and caches results in /tmp/mypy for speed.
